full_name: Randomized primal-dual gradient method for strongly convex finite-sum optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020, Section 5.1, Theorem 5.1

problem.description: Convex finite-sum problem reformulated as a multi-dual-player saddle point problem for the RPDG method.

variable_space.math: X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a closed convex set},\quad Y:=Y_1\times Y_2\times\cdots\times Y_m,\quad Z\equiv X\times Y.

saddle_reformulation.math: \Psi^*:=\min_{x\in X}\left\{h(x)+\mu\nu(x)+\max_{y\in Y}\langle x,Uy\rangle-J(y)\right\},\qquad U:=[I,I,\ldots,I],\qquad J(y):=\sum_{i=1}^m J_i(y_i).

dual_conjugate_definition.math: \text{Let }J_i:Y_i\to\mathbb{R}\text{ be the conjugate functions of }f_i/m\text{ and }Y_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ denote the dual spaces where the gradients of }f_i/m\text{ reside. For the sake of notational convenience, let us denote }J(y):=\sum_{i=1}^m J_i(y_i),\ Y:=Y_1\times Y_2\times\ldots\times Y_m,\text{ and }y=(y_1;y_2;\ldots;y_m)\text{ for any }y_i\in Y_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m.

gap_function.math: Q(\bar z,z):=[h(\bar x)+\mu\nu(\bar x)+\langle\bar x,Uy\rangle-J(y)]-[h(x)+\mu\nu(x)+\langle x,U\bar y\rangle-J(\bar y)].

assumptions.name: simple_term_convexity
assumptions.math: h\text{ is a relatively simple convex function,}

assumptions.name: component_convexity
assumptions.math: f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R},\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ are smooth convex functions with Lipschitz continuous gradient,}

assumptions.name: dual_conjugate_definition
assumptions.math: \text{Let }J_i:Y_i\to\mathbb{R}\text{ be the conjugate functions of }f_i/m\text{ and }Y_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ denote the dual spaces where the gradients of }f_i/m\text{ reside. For the sake of notational convenience, let us denote }J(y):=\sum_{i=1}^m J_i(y_i),\ Y:=Y_1\times Y_2\times\ldots\times Y_m,\text{ and }y=(y_1;y_2;\ldots;y_m)\text{ for any }y_i\in Y_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m.

assumptions.name: dual_strong_convexity
assumptions.math: J_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ are strongly convex with modulus }\sigma_i=m/L_i\text{ w.r.t. }\|\cdot\|_*,

initialization.math: x^0=x^{-1}\in X,\text{ and the nonnegative parameters }\{\tau_t\},\{\eta_t\},\text{ and }\{\alpha_t\}\text{ be given. Set }y_i^0=\frac{1}{m}\nabla f_i(x^0),\quad i=1,\ldots,m.

parameters.name: candidate_dual_update
parameters.math: \hat y_i^t:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y_i\in Y_i}\{\langle-\tilde x^t,y_i\rangle+J_i(y_i)+\tau_t W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i)\},\quad i=1,\ldots,m;\ t=1,\ldots,k.

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Suppose that }\{\tau_t\},\{\eta_t\},\text{ and }\{\alpha_t\}\text{ in the RPDG method are set to }\tau_t=\tau,\eta_t=\eta,\text{ and }\alpha_t=\alpha\text{ for any }t\ge 1\text{ such that }(1-\alpha)(1+\tau)\le p_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ \eta\le\alpha(\mu+\eta),\ \eta\tau p_i\ge 4L_i/m,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ for some }\alpha\in(0,1).\text{ Then, for any }k\ge 1,\ \mathbb{E}[V(x^k,x^*)]\le\left(1+\frac{L_f\alpha}{(1-\alpha)\eta}\right)\alpha^kV(x^0,x^*),\quad \mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar x^k)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\alpha^{k/2}\left(\alpha^{-1}\eta+\frac{3-2\alpha}{1-\alpha}L_f+\frac{2L_f^2\alpha}{(1-\alpha)\eta}\right)V(x^0,x^*),\text{ where }\bar x^k=\left(\sum_{t=1}^k\theta_t\right)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^k(\theta_t x^t)\text{ with }\theta_t=1/\alpha^t,\ \forall t=1,\ldots,k,\text{ and }x^*\text{ denotes the optimal solution of problem (5.1.1), and the expectation is taken w.r.t. }i_1,\ldots,i_k.
main_theorem.rate: Linear in the Bregman distance: O(alpha^k); linear up to square-root exponent for the ergodic primal gap: O(alpha^{k/2}).
main_theorem.measure: Expected Bregman distance to x^* and expected primal optimality gap of the weighted average \bar x^k.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma_5_2_primal_gap_from_saddle_gap
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }(\bar x,\bar y)\in Z\text{ be a given pair of feasible solutions of (5.1.12), and }z^*=(x^*,y^*)\text{ be a pair of optimal solutions of (5.1.12). Then, we have }\Psi(\bar x)-\Psi(x^*)\le Q((\bar x,\bar y),z^*)+\frac{L_f}{2}\|\bar x-x^*\|^2.
key_lemmas.role: Converts the averaged saddle-point gap obtained from Proposition 5.1 into a primal optimality gap.

proof.description: Define \bar y^*=(m^{-1}\nabla f_1(\bar x);\ldots;m^{-1}\nabla f_m(\bar x)) and expand Q((\bar x,\bar y),z^*) using the definition of Q and the max representation of f(x^*).
proof.ref: Proof of Lemma 5.2, first part of displayed chain
proof.math: Q((\bar x,\bar y),z^*)\ge [h(\bar x)+\mu\nu(\bar x)+\langle\bar x,U\bar y^*\rangle-J(\bar y^*)]+\langle\bar x,U(y^*-\bar y^*)\rangle-J(y^*)+J(\bar y^*)-[h(x^*)+\mu\nu(x^*)+\max_{y\in Y}\{\langle x^*,Uy\rangle-J(y)\}]
proof.produces: Lower bound for Q before using conjugacy.

proof.description: Use that J_i are the conjugate functions of f_i to simplify the lower-bound expression from the preceding display; this preserves Q((\bar x,\bar y),z^*) as a lower bound, not an equality.
proof.ref: Proof of Lemma 5.2, second part of displayed chain
proof.math: \Psi(\bar x)-\Psi(x^*)+\langle\bar x,U(y^*-\bar y^*)\rangle-\langle x^*,Uy^*\rangle+f(x^*)+\langle\bar x,U\bar y^*\rangle-f(\bar x)=\Psi(\bar x)-\Psi(x^*)+f(x^*)-f(\bar x)+\langle\bar x-x^*,\nabla f(x^*)\rangle\ge \Psi(\bar x)-\Psi(x^*)-\frac{L_f}{2}\|\bar x-x^*\|^2,
proof.produces: Equation (5.1.35) after rearrangement.

key_lemmas.name: Saddle_gap_nonnegative_at_solution

key_lemmas.name: Lemma_5_3_generalized_prox_inequality
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }U\text{ be a closed convex set and a point }\tilde u\in U\text{ be given. Also let }w:U\to\mathbb{R}\text{ be a convex function and }W(\tilde u,u)=w(u)-w(\tilde u)-\langle w'(\tilde u),u-\tilde u\rangle\text{ for some }w'(\tilde u)\in\partial w(\tilde u).\text{ Assume that }q(u_1)-q(u_2)-\langle q'(u_2),u_1-u_2\rangle\ge \mu_0W(u_2,u_1),\ \forall u_1,u_2\in U,\text{ for some }\mu_0\ge0.\text{ Also assume that }\mu_0+\mu_1+\mu_2\ge0.\text{ If }u^*\in\operatorname{Argmin}\{q(u)+\mu_1w(u)+\mu_2W(\tilde u,u):u\in U\},\text{ then for any }u\in U,\text{ we have }q(u^*)+\mu_1w(u^*)+\mu_2W(\tilde u,u^*)+(\mu_0+\mu_1+\mu_2)W(u^*,u)\le q(u)+\mu_1w(u)+\mu_2W(\tilde u,u).
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the primal and dual one-step inequalities (5.1.43) and (5.1.44).

proof.description: Set phi(u):=q(u)+mu_1 w(u)+mu_2 W(tilde u,u) and write the two Bregman identities used to compare phi at u_1 and u_2.
proof.math: W(\tilde u,u_1)=W(\tilde u,u_2)+\langle W'(\tilde u,u_2),u_1-u_2\rangle+W(u_2,u_1),\qquad w(u_1)=w(u_2)+\langle w'(u_2),u_1-u_2\rangle+W(u_2,u_1).
proof.produces: Bregman three-point identities for W and w.

proof.description: Combine the Bregman identities with the assumed relative strong convexity of q to obtain the displayed lower bound on phi.
proof.produces: Equation (5.1.39) and convexity of phi when mu_0+mu_1+mu_2 >= 0.

proof.description: Use optimality of u^* for (5.1.38), namely <phi'(u^*),u-u^*> >= 0, and combine it with (5.1.39) at (u_1,u_2)=(u,u^*) to derive the prox inequality.
proof.produces: The conclusion of Lemma 5.3 after expanding phi.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma_5_4_conditional_expectation_identities
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }y^t,\tilde y^t,\text{ and }\hat y^t\text{ be defined in (5.1.22), (5.1.23), and (5.1.25), respectively. Then we have, for any }i=1,\ldots,m\text{ and }t=1,\ldots,k,\quad \mathbb{E}_t[W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i^t)]=p_iW_i(y_i^{t-1},\hat y_i^t),\quad \mathbb{E}_t[W_i(y_i^t,y_i)]=p_iW_i(\hat y_i^t,y_i)+(1-p_i)W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i),\text{ for any }y\in Y.
key_lemmas.role: Turns the randomized dual update terms into deterministic weighted Bregman terms in the proof of Lemma 5.5.

proof.description: For (5.1.40), condition on the event i_t=i: y_i^t=\hat y_i^t with conditional probability p_i and y_i^t=y_i^{t-1} with conditional probability 1-p_i; W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i^{t-1})=0.
proof.produces: Equation (5.1.40).

proof.produces: Equation (5.1.41).

proof.description: Combine the primal inequality, the summed dual inequality, and the definition of Q. The mismatch terms involving \tilde y^t and \hat y^t are kept explicitly.
proof.math: Q((x^t,\hat y^t),z)\le \eta_tV(x^{t-1},x)-(\mu+\eta_t)V(x^t,x)-\eta_tV(x^{t-1},x^t)+\sum_{i=1}^m[\tau_tW_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i)-(1+\tau_t)W_i(\hat y_i^t,y_i)-\tau_tW_i(y_i^{t-1},\hat y_i^t)]+\langle\tilde x^t,U(\hat y^t-y)\rangle-\langle x^t,U(\tilde y^t-y)\rangle+\langle x,U(\tilde y^t-\hat y^t)\rangle.
proof.produces: Equation (5.1.45).

proof.description: Record the expectation identities used to convert the hat-y terms and eliminate the final x-coupling term.
proof.math: W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i^t)=0,\ \forall i\ne i_t,\quad \mathbb{E}[\langle x,U(\tilde y^t-\hat y^t)\rangle]=0,\quad \mathbb{E}[\langle\tilde x^t,U\hat y^t\rangle]=\mathbb{E}[\langle\tilde x^t,U\tilde y^t\rangle],\quad \mathbb{E}[W_i(y_i^{t-1},\hat y_i^t)]=\mathbb{E}[p_i^{-1}W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i^t)],\quad \mathbb{E}[W_i(\hat y_i^t,y_i)]=p_i^{-1}\mathbb{E}[W_i(y_i^t,y_i)]-(p_i^{-1}-1)\mathbb{E}[W_i(y_i^{t-1},y_i)].
proof.produces: Expectation substitutions for Eq. (5.1.45).

proof.description: Take expectation in (5.1.45) and substitute the observations to obtain the one-step recursion.
proof.produces: Equation (5.1.42).

key_lemmas.name: Proposition_5_1_weighted_RPDG_bound
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Suppose that }\{\tau_t\},\{\eta_t\},\text{ and }\{\alpha_t\}\text{ in the RPDG method satisfy }\theta_t[p_i^{-1}(1+\tau_t)-1]\le p_i^{-1}\theta_{t-1}(1+\tau_{t-1}),\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ t=2,\ldots,k,\quad \theta_t\eta_t\le\theta_{t-1}(\mu+\eta_{t-1}),\ t=2,\ldots,k,\quad \frac{\eta_k}{4}\ge\frac{L_i(1-p_i)^2}{m\tau_kp_i},\ i=1,\ldots,m,\quad \frac{\eta_{t-1}}{2}\ge\frac{L_i\alpha_t}{m\tau_t p_i}+\frac{(1-p_j)^2L_j}{m\tau_{t-1}p_j},\ i,j\in\{1,\ldots,m\};\ t=2,\ldots,k,\quad \frac{\eta_k}{2}\ge\frac{\sum_{i=1}^m(p_iL_i)}{m(1+\tau_k)},\quad \alpha_t\theta_t=\theta_{t-1},\ t=2,\ldots,k,\text{ for some }\theta_t\ge0,\ t=1,\ldots,k.\text{ Then, for any }k\ge1\text{ and any given }z\in Z,\ \sum_{t=1}^k\theta_t\mathbb{E}[Q((x^t,\hat y^t),z)]\le \eta_1\theta_1V(x^0,x)-(\mu+\eta_k)\theta_k\mathbb{E}[V(x^k,x)]+\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_1[p_i^{-1}(1+\tau_1)-1]W_i(y_i^0,y_i).
key_lemmas.role: Weighted telescoping result used directly in Theorem 5.1.
